```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(herminR)
```

## What MPI measures

For a second-order model in coded units, the Maximal Possible Influence of a
factor is the largest absolute change in the response produced by a one-unit
increase of that factor inside the coded range, with every other factor at its
most favourable level. For factor 3 of response 4 in Otava and Mylona (2020),

$$\mathrm{MPI}_{34} = |\beta_{34}| + |\gamma_{34}| + |\delta_{234}| = 0.2294 + 0.4185 + 0.3706 = 1.0185,$$

with main effect \(\beta_{34} = 0.2294\), quadratic effect
\(\gamma_{34} = 0.4185\) and interaction \(\delta_{234} = 0.3706\)
(their Table 1, bundled as `pastry_table1`).

```{r}
data(pastry_table1)
pastry_table1$y4
mpi(pastry_table1$y4, factors = "x1")
```

Factor `x1` has no term in this model, so its MPI is 0. The `direction` column
says whether the maximal change is an increase or a decrease of the response
when the factor increases (`"either"` when there is no main effect and both
signs are attainable).

## From a fitted model

Any `lm` with `x`, `I(x^2)`, `x:y` or raw `poly()` terms, or an `rsm` fit with
`FO()`/`TWI()`/`PQ()`/`SO()`, can be used directly. Block terms are recognised
as nuisance terms and excluded.

```{r}
data(pastrydough)
fit <- lm(y ~ block + (x1 + x2 + x3)^2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + I(x3^2),
          data = pastrydough)
m <- mpi(fit, bounds = "delta")
m
```

## Interactive explorer

`run_explorer()` opens a Shiny app (needs the shiny package) that runs the
same analysis interactively, from data or coefficients to MPI, uncertainty,
robustness and follow-up. Its *Reproduce* tab gives the R code for what is on
screen.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_explorer()
```

## Several responses

Table 1 of Otava and Mylona (2020) for the four pastry responses is bundled:

```{r}
data(pastry_table1)
m4 <- mpi_multi(pastry_table1, factors = c("x1", "x2", "x3"))
m4
plot(m4, method = "colmax", transpose = TRUE, reorder = FALSE)
```
